objective: Compare blood glucose distributions across Diabetes, Stroke and CKD patient cohorts (age 30-70, glucose>0 & non-missing) with Kruskal-Wallis H test plus Dunn post-hoc (Bonferroni), and produce output.csv / output.png.
status: plan finalized; upstream artifacts (glucose_unified.csv, output.csv, output.png, data_profile.json) independently verified as consistent with this plan

environment.note: imports fail unless sys.path.append of user site-packages is done first (pandas is not in the default site-packages)

inputs.data_quality: Glucose contains 0 sentinels (= missing); no NaN ages observed
age has 8 missing; glucose is float, no zeros; 1 record with age < 30 in raw set
missing encoded as '?'; 3 malformed rows with an extra comma (need repair, e.g. csv reader + column-count fix); bgr has substantial missingness

column_unification.unit_assumption: all three glucose columns already in mg/dL; no rescaling (documented assumption, ranges 44-490 mg/dL are physiologically plausible)
column_unification.coercion: pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') for age and glucose in every source; '?' -> NaN for ARFF

steps: 1. Keep only records with age non-missing and 30 <= age <= 70 (inclusive).
2. Drop records with glucose missing/NaN or glucose == 0 (0 is a missing-value sentinel in Healthcare-Diabetes).
3. Concatenate the three filtered frames and add source label (Diabetes / Stroke / CKD).
filter_plan.verification: independently recomputed from raw files during planning: 1306 / 2885 / 273, total 4464 – matches upstream data_profile.json and glucose_unified.csv

overall_test.name: Kruskal-Wallis H test
overall_test.decision_rule: if p < 0.05 -> proceed to Dunn post-hoc

post_hoc.name: Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction
post_hoc.formula: z_ij = (mean_rank_i - mean_rank_j) / sqrt( (N(N+1)/12 - sum(t^3-t)/(12(N-1))) * (1/n_i + 1/n_j) ), ranks computed on POOLED data with average ties
post_hoc.p_value: two-sided normal: 2 * norm.sf(|z|) (use sf to avoid catastrophic cancellation / underflow)
implementation_notes: Ranks MUST be computed on the pooled sample, not within each group (within-group ranking gives wrong sign/magnitude).
Testing should confirm z values: 23.369293 / -0.437621 / -12.768506, which reproduce upstream output.csv exactly.
Do not use 1 - norm.cdf for |z| > 8: it underflows to 0.0 and loses the reported tiny p-values.

interpretation_targets.group_stats: n, mean, median, std, min, max per group (median Diabetes 125.0, Stroke 92.23, CKD 123.0)
interpretation_targets.headline: Glucose differs significantly across cohorts; Diabetes and CKD are indistinguishable from each other after correction (p_adj = 1.0) but both are markedly higher than Stroke.

visualization_plan.figure: overlaid density histogram of glucose_mgdl for the 3 groups
visualization_plan.annotation: Kruskal-Wallis p-value text placed on the axes (rendered as H = ..., p = ... ; scientific notation for p)
extras: title noting age 30-70 filter and n per group

deliverables.notes: exactly 4 data rows + header; full float precision, no rounding

deliverables.spec: overlaid density histogram, 3 colored groups, p-value annotated

validation_checks.check: no missing/zero glucose in unified data

assumptions_and_risks: Units assumed identical (mg/dL) across all three sources; no conversion applied. If a source were in mmol/L the comparison would be invalid.

CKD 'bgr' is a random glucose measurement while Stroke uses avg_glucose_level and Diabetes a fasting-like Glucose - measurement-type heterogeneity may inflate group differences (interpretation caveat).
Substantial sample-size imbalance (2885 vs 273) - Kruskal-Wallis is rank based so this is acceptable, but CKD estimates have wider CIs.
Records from the three datasets are independent patients; no de-duplication across datasets attempted.
Dunn p-values for very large |z| are below float reproducibility limits; using norm.sf keeps them (2.6e-120, 7.4e-37) rather than 0.0.

handoff.next_nodes: executor (compute tests + plot) and reporter (summarize); this plan contains exact formulas, expected numbers and validation checks to self-verify execution.
